description: LAYA (Local AI Yield Augmentation) capability demonstration — shows LLM-assisted enterprise knowledge analysis using existing local models. Uses Meridian Financial Services (MFS) demo data.

scenarios.question: Summarize the payment timeout spike incident (INC0080101) and its resolution
scenarios.note: Traces INC0080101 → mfs-payment-gateway → CHG0090101 tokenization deployment → MR !301 → PAY-101

scenarios.question: Why was HSM key rotation chosen over software-based key management for PCI DSS compliance?
scenarios.note: Draws from Confluence PCI DSS checklist, PAY-202 story description, and architecture docs

scenarios.question: Is the Payment Gateway V2 release ready for production?
scenarios.note: Checks: TC-PAY-007 IN_PROGRESS (blocker), TC-PAY-008 NOT_RUN (blocker), all pipelines green, Grafana dashboards configured

scenarios.question: Generate a runbook for handling payment gateway timeout incidents
scenarios.note: Uses incident history, Grafana dashboards, pod topology, DB connection info, and existing Confluence runbook as inputs

scenarios.question: Assess the risk of deploying the fraud scoring model v2 (FRD-101)
scenarios.note: Analyzes: blast radius across mfs-fraud-engine dependents, previous incident INC0080201 (false positive spike), Kafka consumer impact, model rollback plan

scenarios.question: What is mfs-common-libs and how does it connect to other systems?
scenarios.note: Explains the shared library's role: AuthClient used by all services, AuditLogger for compliance, MetricsCollector for observability

scenarios.question: What are the testing coverage gaps across the MFS platform?
scenarios.note: Identifies: settlement batch (TC-PAY-007 incomplete), SAR reporting (TC-FRD-007 not run), mfs-customer-portal has no test cases

scenarios.question: Summarize the deployment and incident trends for Meridian Financial Services this quarter
scenarios.note: Aggregates: deployment frequency, incident rate, mean time to recovery, change failure rate from ServiceNow and GitLab data

scenarios.question: Compare the architectural patterns used in the payment gateway vs fraud detection platform
scenarios.note: Compares architecture, patterns, libraries, and design decisions between mfs-payment-gateway and mfs-fraud-engine

scenarios.question: Explain the end-to-end data flow from a payment transaction to fraud score to settlement
scenarios.note: Traces data flow: PaymentService ingests transaction, FraudScoringEngine evaluates risk, SettlementBatchProcessor completes settlement

scenarios.question: Predict which components are most likely to cause an outage based on recent change velocity and test coverage
scenarios.note: Computes risk scores using change frequency, test coverage gaps, incident history, and dependency complexity for each component

scenarios.question: Generate a PCI DSS compliance evidence report for the payment tokenization path
scenarios.note: Maps PCI DSS requirements to evidence: TokenizationService encryption, token vault access controls, HSM key management procedures

scenarios.question: Analyze team workload distribution and identify bottleneck risks for the Q4 release
scenarios.note: Analyzes story point distribution, assignment density, and cross-team dependencies across Q4 sprints

scenarios.question: What if we migrate from PostgreSQL to CockroachDB for the payment database - what's the impact analysis?
scenarios.note: Simulates PostgreSQL to CockroachDB migration: identifies all services using pghost-prod-01, schema compatibility issues, connection string changes, and phased migration plan
